candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L, respectively, for Cyanide.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These proposed numeric limits are the enforceable comparison values for Cyanide; interpreting daily maximum vs monthly average, units, or whether draft-proposed limits are treated as applicable would change which limit applies to a given measurement and whether it is compared for compliance.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall have a 1-year compliance schedule to achieve final limitations for Cyanide pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A compliance schedule implies interim versus final limitation periods; different readings of when final limits take effect would change which numeric limit applies (A), what monitoring or reporting is required during the schedule (B), and how missing or interim-period results should be classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permit will require compliance schedule reports.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance schedule reports constitute a monitoring or reporting obligation during the schedule period affects which requirements are deemed applicable for Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Technology based pollutants; BOD5 and TSS, are proposed to be monitored five times per week, with sampling on at least five different days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated frequency and day-distribution rule determine whether BOD5 and TSS monitoring was required for each week or period; alternate readings of 'proposed' status or the five-different-days constraint would change obligation evaluations.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored continuously using a totalizing meter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Continuous flow monitoring establishes a different monitoring obligation than periodic sampling; interpreting this as the operative flow requirement affects whether flow monitoring was required at a given time.

candidates.exact_span: Sample type for BOD5 and TSS is 12-Hr composite.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required sample type is part of the monitoring obligation; a different interpretation of composite sampling requirements could change whether reported samples satisfy the applicable monitoring requirement.

candidates.exact_span: The monitoring frequencies of daily for TRC and five times per week for E. coli, pH and flow are consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage assigns daily monitoring to TRC and five-times-per-week monitoring to E. coli, pH, and flow, but conflicts with the earlier statement that flow is monitored continuously; resolving which flow frequency applies changes monitoring-obligation computations.

candidates.exact_span: Report requirements of once per week for TDS is also consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describing TDS as a weekly report requirement rather than a sampled limit-bearing parameter affects whether an enforceable numeric limit applies (A) and whether a weekly reporting obligation exists (B).

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will not propose any WET limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicit absence of WET numeric limits means no enforceable WET concentration limit is available for compliance comparison; treating WET results as limit-bearing versus monitoring-only would change applicable-limit determinations.

candidates.exact_span: However, continuation of WET monitoring is proposed in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Continued WET monitoring without numeric limits creates monitoring obligations without ordinary numeric compliance comparisons; interpretation affects whether WET testing was required (B) and how no-limit or pass/fail WET outcomes are classified when numeric results are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: When the critical dilution is equal to or less than 10%, in lieu of the 7-day chronic test, a 48-hour acute test may be run using a 10:1 acute to chronic ratio; 23.4% rounded to the nearest whole number 23%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The critical-dilution threshold and optional acute-versus-chronic test selection determine which WET test type is required; different readings of CD=2.34%, the 10% threshold, or permissive 'may be run' language would change applicable monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall conduct a 48-hour acute test using Daphnia pulex once per quarter, and a 48-hour acute test using Pimephales promelas once per quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These species-specific quarterly acute-test requirements define enforceable WET monitoring obligations; interpreting frequency, species, or test duration differently would change which WET monitoring was required in each quarter.

candidates.exact_span: After the first four quarters without failures, the permittee may apply for a frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frequency reduction is conditional and not automatic; whether monitoring remained quarterly or was reduced after four passing quarters affects obligation applicability (B) and how missing later tests are classified as not required versus inadequately documented (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any failure afterwards shall re-establish all tests for both species to once per quarter for the remainder of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A post-failure reinstatement rule makes monitoring frequency depend on test-failure history; different interpretations of what counts as a failure or when reinstatement triggers would change which quarterly WET tests were required.

candidates.exact_span: The test series will be 10%, 13%, 17%, 23% and 31%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The prescribed dilution series is part of the WET testing protocol; alternate readings of required dilutions or rounding would change whether conducted tests satisfied the monitoring requirement.
